title: Power & Taylor Series
summary: A power series $\sum c_n(x-a)^n$ converges on an interval set by its radius $R$ (found via the ratio test). Within $R$ it represents a function you can differentiate and integrate term by term; Taylor series extend the polynomial idea to infinitely many terms.

power series.in_class: $\sum c_n(x-a)^n$; a function of $x$ where it converges.

radius of convergence.plain: Half-width of the interval where it converges.

interval of convergence.plain: All $x$ for which the series converges.
interval of convergence.in_class: Center $\pm R$, with endpoints checked separately.

center a.plain: The point the powers are measured from.

term-by-term.in_class: Legal within the radius of convergence.

geometric building block.in_class: A source series to manipulate into others.

concept_sections.heading: Radius via the ratio test
concept_sections.explanation: Apply the ratio test to $\sum c_n(x-a)^n$ treating $x$ as fixed: convergence requires the limiting ratio $<1$, which solves to $|x-a|<R$.

concept_sections.heading: Interval and endpoints
concept_sections.explanation: The series converges on $(a-R,a+R)$; the endpoints $x=a\pm R$ must be tested individually (they can converge, diverge, or converge conditionally).

concept_sections.heading: Building new series
concept_sections.explanation: Start from $\dfrac{1}{1-x}=\sum x^n$ ($|x|<1$) and substitute or manipulate to get others (e.g. $\dfrac{1}{1+x^2}$, then integrate for $\arctan$).

concept_sections.heading: Term-by-term calculus
concept_sections.explanation: Inside the radius, a power series can be differentiated and integrated term by term, producing new series with the same radius — a powerful way to find sums and antiderivatives.

concept_sections.heading: Taylor series representation
concept_sections.explanation: Extending Taylor polynomials to infinitely many terms gives $f(x)=\sum\dfrac{f^{(n)}(a)}{n!}(x-a)^n$, valid where the remainder $\to0$. The classics ($e^x,\sin,\cos$) converge for all $x$.

real_world_examples.title: Representing functions in software
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: Its power series $x-\tfrac{x^2}{2}+\cdots$ evaluates it term by term.

real_world_examples.title: Solving differential equations
real_world_examples.scenario: Some ODEs have no elementary solution.
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: A power-series ansatz builds the solution coefficient by coefficient.

Find the radius of convergence of $\sum x^n$.
